question: A textile mill's floor report is 10 times the force taken by one loom frame, expressed in kilonewtons. A frame carries two identical beaters, so it takes twice the corrected force of a single beater. For one beater the corrected force is the driving force plus 20 N for the return-spring preload. That beater drives a mass of 193000 g at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 230 and 73 exactly. The mill's overhead lighting is rated at 400 W. What does the floor report give, in kN?

A school lab's summary is 11 times a paired-bench figure, expressed in kilojoules. A paired-bench figure is twice a single bench's balance, since the benches are always used in pairs. One bench's balance is the glider's kinetic energy less 29 J drawn by the air blower. The glider has a mass of 3 kg, and the lab's extractor fan draws 45 W. The glider's speed, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 9 times the value, plus 18, equals exactly 0. What is the lab's summary, in kJ?

A packaging plant's final tally adds 20 N for the frame's own reaction to 5 times a line total. A line total is 11 times one pusher's corrected force, and a pusher's corrected force is the force on its carton plus 21 N for the belt drag. The carton has a mass of 12 kg. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 3 times the sum of the two ramp settings, which read 8 and 3. What is the plant's final tally, in N?

A foundry's test record ends with twice a single trolley's kinetic energy, less 5 J absorbed by the buffer. The trolley has a mass of 43 kg, and the foundry's inspection lamp draws 70 W. Its speed in metres per second is found by taking a calibration reading and subtracting 7. That calibration reading comes from a chart on which a plotted quantity equals 2 times the cube of the dial setting minus 5 times the square of the dial setting, and the reading is the second-order rate of change of that plotted quantity with respect to the dial setting, evaluated at a dial setting of 2. What does the test record end with, in J?

A brewery's annual figure is 9 times its monthly figure, and the monthly figure is 9 times a weekly figure. A weekly figure covers 3 identical crate runs, so it is 3 times the energy of a single run. A crate has a mass of 41000 g. Its speed along the roller table, in metres per second, is numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 210 and 178 exactly. What is the brewery's annual figure, in J?

A test house's report gives twice the energy of a single carriage, in kilojoules, because the house runs a mirrored pair of tracks. The carriage has a mass of 43 kg, and the house's ventilation fan draws 90 W. The carriage's speed, in metres per second, is 3 times the total that the track meter accumulates between the 0th and the 1st second of a run. The meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 3 times t squared plus 2 times t. What does the test house's report give, in kJ?

A bicycle factory's shift figure is 6 times a single station's total, expressed in kilojoules. A station's total is the test carriage's kinetic energy plus 19 J drawn by its indexing motor. The carriage has a mass of 58 kg, and the station's inspection lamp is rated at 55 W. The carriage's speed, in metres per second, is numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 100 and 397 exactly. What is the factory's shift figure, in kJ?

A tunnelling contractor's summary is 3 times a machine's net figure. The net figure is the force driving the cutter head, expressed in kilonewtons, less 22 kN allowed for the thrust ring and a further 20 kN allowed for the tail seal. The cutter head has a mass of 140 kg, and the tunnel bore is 6 m across. The head's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 4 times the sum of the two feed-dial settings, which read 4 and 8. What is the contractor's summary, in kN?

A print works' hall figure adds 13 N for the frame's load-cell offset to the combined force of its 4 identical banks. Each bank contains 12 identical rollers pushing together. One roller drives a mass of 57 kg at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 236 and 310 exactly. The works' dryer is rated at 8 kW. What is the hall figure, in N?

A funicular operator's fleet figure is 10 times a line's figure, and a line's figure is 4 times one car's booked energy. A car's booked energy is its kinetic energy in kilojoules plus 22 kJ drawn by the haulage house. Each car has a mass of 33000 g on the scale model used for the estimate. A car's speed, in metres per second, is 4 times the sum of the two gradient-dial readings, which are 6 and 11. What is the operator's fleet figure, in kJ?

A dockside hoist meters its drive through a lift, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 1 times t squared plus 0 times t. The hoist takes the total accumulated between the 1st and the 4th second and adds 7 to obtain the load's acceleration in metres per second squared. The load has a mass of 37000 g. The dock's summary takes the driving force in kilonewtons, adds 16 kN for the jib's own weight, and then adds a further 3 kN for the counterweight tie. What does the dock's summary give, in kN?

A go-kart workshop tests a flywheel puck of mass 8000 g on a level bench. The puck's speed, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 10 times the value, plus 24, equals exactly 0. The bench sheet takes the puck's kinetic energy, adds 23 J drawn by the release solenoid, and then subtracts 10 J recovered at the catcher. The workshop runs 8 identical benches, and its report gives 8 times the single-bench figure. What does the report give, in J?

A wave-tank facility's weekly figure is 7 times its daily figure, and the daily figure is a float's kinetic energy in kilojoules plus 7 kJ drawn by the paddle drive. The float has a mass of 19 kg. Its speed, in metres per second, is found by taking a meter total and subtracting 11. That total is what the tank's meter accumulates between the 2nd and the 3rd second of a surge, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 3 times t squared plus 2 times t. What is the facility's weekly figure, in kJ?

A dredger's balance sheet is the frame force in kilonewtons, less 27 kN allowed for the pontoon tie. The frame carries 4 identical rams, so the frame force is 4 times one ram's corrected force, and a ram's corrected force is the force on its load plus 7 N for the seal drag. That load has a mass of 103 kg. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 14 times the value, plus 48, equals exactly 0. What does the balance sheet give, in kN?

A ski resort's day figure is a lift total less 16 kJ credited back by the regenerative drive. The lift total is 5 times a bank's figure, and a bank's figure is 4 times a single chair's energy in kilojoules. A loaded chair has a mass of 17 kg on the scale model used for the estimate. A chair's speed, in metres per second, is 8 times the sum of the two haul-dial settings, which read 7 and 1. What is the resort's day figure, in kJ?

A cable-car company's annual figure is 9 times its monthly figure, and the monthly figure is 9 times the energy of a single cabin, in kilojoules. A cabin has a mass of 25000 g on the scale rig used for the estimate, and the rig's control lamp draws 30 W. The cabin's distance along the rig track, in metres, is 5 times the cube of the elapsed seconds minus 1 times the square of the elapsed seconds. The company uses how fast the cabin is moving at the instant 1 second after release. What is the company's annual figure, in kJ?

A ropeway test rig meters its winch through a pull, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 1 times t squared plus 2 times t. The carrier's speed, in metres per second, equals the total the meter accumulates between the 1st and the 3rd second. The carrier has a mass of 19 kg, and the rig's span is 120 m. The rig makes 11 identical pulls in a session, and the log then subtracts 11 J for the brake bleed and adds 5 J for the beacon. What does the log record for a session, in J?

A cannery receives 132 lids of one type and 359 of another, and it packs them into identical cases using the largest case size that divides both counts exactly. A pusher then drives a tray of mass 40000 g at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, equal to 5 times that case size. The line's log subtracts 8 N for the rail friction and adds 24 N for the return-spring preload. The line's steriliser is rated at 12 kW. Ten identical pushers work the floor, and the log reports 10 times the single-pusher figure. What does the log report, in N?

A hydraulic test bench meters its pump through a stroke, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 2 times t squared plus 7 times t. The bench takes the total accumulated between the 0th and the 2nd second, subtracts 11, and uses the result as the ram's speed in metres per second. The ram carries a striker of mass 26 kg, and the bench's extraction fan draws 220 W. Four identical benches run at the same time. How much kinetic energy do the four strikers carry altogether, in kJ?

A logistics hub's regional figure is 9 times a depot's figure, and a depot's figure is 4 times a bay's total in kilojoules. A bay's total covers 6 identical parcel launches, so it is 6 times the energy of one parcel. A parcel has a mass of 7 kg. Its speed, in metres per second, equals the total the chute meter accumulates between the 0th and the 2nd second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 2 times t squared plus 6 times t. What is the hub's regional figure, in kJ?

A drone club's season figure is 6 times a meet figure, and a meet figure is 5 times a single flight's booked energy. A flight's booked energy is the drone's kinetic energy in kilojoules plus 21 kJ drawn by the ground station. The drone has a mass of 2000 g. Its speed, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 11 times the value, plus 30, comes to exactly 0. What is the club's season figure, in kJ?

A ropemaking machine drives a carriage of mass 61000 g along its bed. The carriage's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is twice the sum of the two feed-dial readings, which are 2 and 8. The machine's log takes the driving force and adds 14 N for the guide-roller drag. Expressed in kilonewtons, the works' balance then subtracts 10 kN allowed for the bed's own restraint. What does the works' balance give, in kN?

A forge's control sheet builds a base figure by adding together the values of 2 times k minus 1, for each whole number k from 1 to 6. The hammer's impact speed, in metres per second, is that base figure with 7 subtracted and then 27 added. The hammer has a mass of 25 kg, and the forge's extraction duct is 12 m long. The record takes the hammer's kinetic energy and subtracts 22 J absorbed by the anvil block. What does the record give, in J?

A glassworks receives 306 blanks of one size and 156 of another, and it packs them into identical crates using the largest crate size that divides both counts exactly. A test gob of mass 60 kg then travels along the runway at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that crate size. The works handles 8 identical gobs at once, and the log subtracts 19 J absorbed by the shear. The works' annealing lehr is rated at 40 kW. Expressed in kilojoules, the site sheet then subtracts 17 kJ credited back by the heat-recovery unit. What does the site sheet give, in kJ?

A laboratory shaker drives a mass of 5 kg on its table. That mass's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 9 times the value, plus 20, equals exactly 0. Two identical shakers are bolted to each bench, and 9 benches run at once, so the floor takes 9 times the force of a single bench pair. The floor log then adds 15 N for the frame preload and subtracts 28 N for the isolator reaction. What does the floor log record, in N?
